entities.name: Infante Ferdinand, Duke of Viseu
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Infante Ferdinand, Duke of Viseu and Beja was the third son of Edward, King of Portugal, and Eleanor of Aragon.

Born in unknown year, he became Duke of Viseu and Beja upon his father's death in 1438. His rule was marked by conflicts with the Holy Roman Emperor, Sigismund, and the Portuguese nobility.

Ferdinand played a key role in the Portuguese Reconquista, leading military campaigns against the Moors in the Algarve region.

His legacy extended to the Portuguese monarchy, as he was succeeded by his son, Afonso V, who went on to become King of Portugal in 1443.

A striking example of his military prowess was his victory at the Battle of Aljubarrota in 1471, which secured the Portuguese control over the Algarve.

The Infante's significance lies in his role as a unifying force for the Portuguese nobility and his contributions to the country's military expansion during the Reconquista.
